text:
morgan: Quick design check — playing with the playground's structured results panel. Focus jumps weird when you open a tool result, and the primary action button steals keyboard focus from the run history list. Repro: tab through runs → open result → tab again lands on action button instead of back to runs or result content.

alex: Ugh yes saw that. On mac + Chrome. I think it's because we programmatically focus the action to announce it for screen readers. But we might be over-eager.

jules: Screenshot? And which button is "primary action" here — the Invoke / Re-run or the Copy JSON?

morgan: Attached screenshot in thread (attached: focused-button.png). Primary is the small kebab -> Open tool result -> then the big "Run again" CTA. The problem is when you close the result panel and press Shift+Tab we don't land on the run in the list, we land on the invisible focus trap briefly.

sam: Can repro on Win/Firefox too. Also keyboard users expect the focus to return to the initiating element (the run item) when a modal/panel closes. We aren't doing that consistently for the slide-over.

lee: Proposed fix: when panel opens, don't auto-focus the action button. Instead use aria-live to announce "Result opened: Schema validation passed" and leave focus where it is, or move focus into the panel container with a logical first element (like the result header link). That would make tab order predictable.

alex: Agree. Also we should add skip-to-results link at top of run history for power users — visible on focus only.

jules: Minor copy nit: current button says "Run again with tools" — super wordy. Shorten to "Re-run" and put a tooltip for the longer explanation. For a11y, ensure the tooltip is accessible (aria-describedby).

morgan: Another accessibility nit: the structured output JSON viewer doesn't expose roles for nested function outputs. Screen reader reads the whole blob as one region. Suggest adding role="tree" + aria-labels for each function result summary so users can navigate by section.

sam: That aligns with our goal to make tool-calling outputs skimmable. We could render each function result as a summary/button (collapsible) with aria-expanded toggles. That also reduces noise for long outputs.

designbot: Reminder: design review checklist item 4.3 requires keyboard focus return on slide-overs. See https://redwood.design/reviews/checklist#4.3

alex: Implementation question — if we move focus into panel header, should we programmatically set focus to the header link? That still feels like programmatic focus but is more predictable than forcing CTA focus. Thoughts?

jules: Programmatic focus is fine if it's the first logical interactive element and we document it. The anti-pattern is moving focus to something unexpected (like a big CTA you don't need to act on).

lee: I'll prototype a variant: on open -> focus the heading link (tabbable) -> ensure first Tab lands on content, not run history. On close -> focus back to the originating run item. Also add an offscreen skip-link to jump to run history.

morgan: Sounds good. Also let's add a small visual focus ring to the run items (2px) — they currently have faint outline which is easy to miss.

sam: Can we add automated unit tests for focus return? We have some puppeteer tests for the playground; add one that opens result panel and asserts document.activeElement after close equals the run button.

alex: Yep I'll add tests. Also will update copy to "Re-run" and wire tooltip aria-describedby.

jules: One more tiny thing — color contrast for the collapsed summary chevron is 3.8:1 on some themes. Needs to be >=4.5:1.

lee: Noted. I'll adjust the chevron to #2b2f33 on dark theme.

morgan: Thanks all. Can we ship the prototype to the dev sandbox so PM/CS can validate before merging?

alex: Will create PR and deploy to sandbox. PR will include accessibility checklist and puppeteer test.

designbot: PR created by alex: https://git.internal/redwood/playground/pull/4821 — deployment to sandbox scheduled. :rocket:
